subject: Information Theory
title: Quorum Sensing
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Quorum Sensing.

hook.text: Bacteria count their neighbors before attacking. Below threshold: hide. Above threshold: strike together. It's a vote.

buildup.text: Quorum sensing: bacteria release signaling molecules. When concentration exceeds a threshold, collective action begins.

discovery.text: This is a distributed threshold detector. Each bacterium contributes a signal; the collective decides when to act.

twist.text: Some bacteria cheat—they respond to signals without producing them. Free riders exploit the communication system.

climax.text: Quorum sensing shows that even single-celled organisms implement information-processing networks.

punchline.text: Bacteria vote with molecules. The majority rules.

quiz.question: What triggers collective behavior in quorum sensing?
options: Signal molecule concentration exceeding a threshold
